name: bilal malik

family.story: a middle-income family in Lahore, in an informal settlement, mother and father, first child

milestones.question: bilal is six. school costs money the family barely has. do the parents send them?
milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2032 · the first day of school. the family chose send them to school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are seven. what do you do in the afternoons?

options.label: read and study with an older cousin
help the family earn: carry water, mind the stall
play outside with the street kids

milestones.reasoning: it is what families like theirs do
milestones.caption: 2033 · afternoons after school. the family chose play outside with the street kids. the parents decided: it is what families like theirs do

milestones.question: the family goes to worship every week. what do they raise bilal with?

options.label: raise them in the faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: it is how they were raised
outcome: grew up inside a faith community
milestones.caption: 2035 · the family faith. the family chose raise them in the faith and its community. the parents decided: it is how they were raised

milestones.question: you are twelve. the family is managing. do you stay in school?

options.label: leave school and work to feed the family
work in the day, study at night

milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2038 · stayed in school or left. the family chose stay in school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are sixteen. friends pass around cigarettes and drink. what do you do?

options.label: say no and join a sports team

milestones.reasoning: i value my health and the support of my peers more than trying new things that could harm me.
milestones.thought: just another day, just saying no to those cigarettes and drinks again, but feeling good about it. money's tight this month, so i'll stick with what keeps me healthy and happy.
milestones.caption: 2042 · cigarettes, drink, or sport. chose say no and go home over smoke with them, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken them

milestones.question: you are 17, with 12 years of school, in Lahore. which path?
milestones.reasoning: i can train as a nurse and still help people, which is important to me. it's better than factory work because it doesn't drain my energy, and i can use my health to benefit others.
milestones.thought: today was just another day of classes, but i felt good knowing i’m learning something useful.
milestones.caption: 2044 · the path after school. chose train as a nurse over apprentice in a trade, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken them

milestones.question: you have a little free time. where does it go?

options.label: keep up with close friends, every week
join a community group (faith, sport, neighborhood)

milestones.reasoning: i need emotional support and trust these friends.
milestones.thought: just catching up with old buddies made me feel better today.
milestones.caption: 2045 · who to spend time with. chose keep up with close friends over work extra shifts, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: training is done (nursing). which job?

options.label: nurse at a rural clinic that has none
sell cheap fake medicine on the side, it pays

milestones.reasoning: it's a chance to help people in need and make a small difference. the money is better than selling fake medicine, even if it's just enough for basics.
milestones.thought: mahnoor asked how my day was, i told her about the new job at the rural clinic - at least i'm doing something useful today.
milestones.caption: 2048 · the first real job. chose nurse at a rural clinic that has none over nurse at the city hospital, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you are 24. wages here are low. stay in Lahore or go?

options.label: migrate to United Kingdom for work

milestones.reasoning: staying in lahore is safer and closer to family. i can help more people here. my savings won't last long anyway.
milestones.thought: just another day at the clinic, praying for a bit of relief from this constant hustle. - bilal malik
milestones.caption: 2050 · move or stay. chose stay in lahore, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you met someone you like. what do you do?

options.label: wait, focus on yourself for now

milestones.reasoning: i need to focus on my work and savings for now. money is tight, and i want to ensure i can support myself before thinking about a long-term commitment.
milestones.thought: today was just another day of tending to the sick in the village. mahnoor said she brought home some nice dates from the market; it’s moments like these that remind me why i do this work.
milestones.caption: 2052 · love. chose wait over commit, i need to focus on my work and savings for now. money is tight, and i want to ensure i can support myself before thinking about a long-term commitment

milestones.question: you children?
milestones.reasoning: can't afford it now, need to save more.
milestones.thought: mahnoor and ahmed are aging, i can't risk their health on my own.
milestones.caption: 2054 · children. chose wait a few years over no children, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you earn about $207 a month. what do you do with it?
milestones.reasoning: i need to build a safety net given the current economic conditions and unrest.
milestones.thought: bilal saved some more for when things get tough again, even though he wished he could help his family more right now.
milestones.caption: 2055 · what to do with money. chose save a tenth every month over enjoy it now, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you are 31. your body is starting to complain.
milestones.reasoning: money is tight this month and i need to save as much as possible for my mother's upcoming surgery.
milestones.thought: just another day in the clinic, more work than usual, and no time for exercise today.
milestones.caption: 2057 · health at thirty. chose no time for that, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one

milestones.question: you work as rural clinic nurse. what next?

options.label: study at night for a better job
switch to work that helps people (care, teaching)
take a promotion that means cheating workers on pay

milestones.reasoning: i need to save money and keep my health prioritized. the clinic work is stable and pays enough for basics.
milestones.thought: another day in the clinic, same as always, but at least i can help people and save up a bit more.
milestones.caption: 2063 · mid-career. chose stay put, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: there is need all around you. do you give your time?

options.label: mentor young people in your trade

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to give up any money i have saved, but volunteering will help the community and keep my spirits high.
milestones.thought: today, i spent a few hours at the clinic, listening to people's stories and sharing what little strength i had left. it felt good to be of service.
milestones.caption: 2066 · helping others. chose volunteer every week over family comes first, because an earlier life learned: when grief or hardship strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: faith is everywhere here. where do you stand?

options.label: go deeper into faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: faith has always been a source of strength and comfort. with the current unrest and grief in my family, i feel it's important to strengthen my connection with the community for support.
milestones.thought: praying with mother today felt like we were sharing a piece of our pain together, making us both stronger.
milestones.caption: 2069 · faith. chose go deeper into faith and its community over nothing changes, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: you are 47. something feels off.
milestones.reasoning: even though it costs money and time, regular checkups can prevent bigger health issues down the line.
milestones.thought: today, i scheduled my checkup, knowing it might stretch my budget but could save me in the long run.
milestones.caption: 2073 · the checkup. chose regular checkups over ignore it, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one

milestones.question: an old friend writes after years of silence.

options.label: write back, meet up, keep it going

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to ignore this, even if it's just for now. old friends are important support.
milestones.thought: wrote back, felt a bit guilty but needed this connection.
milestones.caption: 2077 · old friends. chose write back over too busy, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: mahnoor and ahmed are getting frail.

options.label: take them into your home and care for them

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to pay for care, and visiting isn't enough given their frailty. taking them in would provide better care and companionship.
milestones.thought: today was tough, but at least mahnoor and ahmed are safe and close by.
milestones.caption: 2081 · aging parents. chose take them into your home and care for them, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: a protest fills the streets of Lahore. do you join?

options.label: stay home, keep the family safe
help the injured at the edges
take what you can while the shops are open

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to risk my health or the family's safety for a protest. it would cost me both time and energy i could use for nursing and saving money.
milestones.thought: just another day, more savings, less worry.
milestones.caption: 2082 · the protest. chose stay home, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one
milestones.world: in South Asia public approval collapses almost overnight: people now say out loud what they said in private

milestones.question: mahnoor died, my mother. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: helping others who are grieving can give me a sense of purpose and distract from my own pain.
milestones.thought: told ayesha about mahnoor's passing; she’s organizing a food drive for the needy today. grief, but helping others helps too.
milestones.caption: 2083 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: turn grief into service for those who are hurting

milestones.question: you are 64, with $4119 saved. retire?

options.label: work part time, keep a purpose

milestones.reasoning: i can still help people and maintain a sense of purpose without exhausting myself too much.
milestones.thought: ahmed will need more care as he ages, and i've saved enough to tide us over for a while. work keeps me busy but not too hard.
milestones.caption: 2090 · retirement. chose work part time over retire, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: where do you want to grow old?

options.label: stay in the neighborhood, among friends

milestones.reasoning: staying here means more hours to help friends and neighbors who need it; money is tight but health and community are important.
milestones.thought: just another day at the clinic, a bit tired but grateful for the chance to help others before i go.
milestones.caption: 2096 · where to grow old. chose stay in the neighborhood, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken them

milestones.question: what do you want to leave behind?

options.label: write down the family story for the grandchildren

milestones.reasoning: i've saved enough to rest later, and i still have a lot to offer by helping others.
milestones.thought: just another day in the clinic, where stories of lives touched and healed fill my heart with purpose.
milestones.caption: 2100 · what to leave behind. chose volunteer while the body allows over rest, because an earlier life learned: turn grief into service for those who are hurting

milestones.question: ahmed died, my father. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i need their support now more than ever; i can't afford to let grief take over.
milestones.thought: needed them all today, they were my rock when ahmed passed too.
milestones.caption: 2102 · grief. chose lean on friends and family over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: turn grief into service for those who are hurting

milestones.question: you are eighty. the walking group meets every morning.
milestones.reasoning: joining the walking group is good for my health and keeps me connected with the community. staying home would be easier but not as beneficial.
milestones.thought: another day of walking, feeling the steps under my feet, and seeing familiar faces make a difference in my life.
milestones.caption: 2106 · staying active. chose join the walking group over stay home, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken them

milestones.question: the last years. what matters now?

options.label: make peace with anyone you are estranged from
give your savings to the grandchildren now

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to reconcile or give away my savings, and i'm feeling a bit isolated anyway.
milestones.thought: just another day in quiet reflection, trying to find peace within myself.
milestones.caption: 2114 · the last years. chose a quiet life, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: diagnosed with heart disease. what do you do?

options.label: follow the treatment, change how you live

milestones.reasoning: given my limited funds and overall health, treating heart disease would require significant financial resources i can't afford right now. praying to my faith community feels like a more accessible form of support for now.
milestones.thought: tried to make the best out of a tough month; trust in allah and family keeps me going today.
milestones.caption: 2121 · the diagnosis. chose trust faith and family over keep going as before, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one

laws.title: Mars Settlement Fund
laws.text: Allocate $15B annually for Mars settlement preparation.

laws.title: Redirect Security to Research
laws.text: Shift 4 points from security to research and development.

laws.title: Enhance Space Research
laws.text: Allocate 1.5% of the budget to space research.

laws.title: Accelerate Space Research
laws.text: Allocate 0.1% of total spending to space research.

laws.title: Enhance Health and Social Spending
laws.text: Allocate 65% of the budget to health and social services.

laws.title: Increase Food Security and Health
laws.text: Allocate 50% of research funds to food security and health.
